mechanism: A structured, verifiable proof that a downstream consumer's rejection of an artifact is grounded in a specific clause of the {{accept_spec}} it was measured against. When a consumer returns a rejection through a Solver's Feedback surface, the rejection must carry a FailureTrace naming the violated clause, citing the evidence, and identifying the evaluator. The upstream Solver uses this trace to distinguish genuine structural feedback from fabricated penalties or hallucinated critique. Trace invalidity (a cited clause that does not exist, evidence that does not match the artifact, or a forged evaluator identity) causes the feedback to be dropped rather than absorbed.
gloss: Structured proof of which AcceptSpec clause a rejected artifact violated — the evidence the Receptivity Gate verifies
invariants: Clause-specific: the trace names exactly one {{accept_spec}} clause per violation, not a generic 'doesn't meet bar'.
Evidence-bound: the violation claim is paired with citeable evidence from the artifact.
Signed and timed: the trace carries the evaluator's cryptographic identity and the time of signing.
failure_modes: Ghost clauses: the trace cites an AcceptSpec clause that does not exist (detectable via schema lookup).
Evidence fabrication: the trace cites evidence the artifact does not contain (detectable via content hash).
Identity spoofing: the evaluator signature is invalid (detectable via signature verification).

Identity replay: a valid `evaluator_ref` is reused on a fabricated trace. Signature verification establishes the identity, not that this trace was signed by it — nothing binds the signature to the trace's contents.
Clause-dancing: the consumer rejects for clause A while the real objection is clause B they did not invoke — no trace schema catches this by itself.
Evidence too weak to entail: the cited evidence exists and does not establish the violation. All three invariants pass — they establish that citations resolve, not that they entail.

accept_spec_ref.description: sema_id of the AcceptSpec the artifact was measured against

violated_clause.description: Identifier of the specific clause claimed violated

evidence.description: Citeable evidence from the artifact supporting the violation claim

evaluator_ref.description: Signed identity of the evaluator asserting the violation

severity.description: Whether the violation halts progress or is informational

signed_at.description: When the evaluator signed. Without it a signature cannot be checked against the key's validity at the time, so a revoked key voids every trace it ever signed.
